These fixtures follow the shapes the D8 tmux 3.8 probe printed (reviews/d8-probe-tmux.log, run 2026-11-05 on a private
server). They were written by hand for the spec; no tmux was run while writing them. Pids, paths, session names and
window ids are placeholders.

What the probe saw (and the fixtures copy):
  split_window.txt          `split-window -h -d -P -F '#{pane_id}\t#{pane_pid}'` printed `%1<TAB>58283`, and the active
                            pane stayed `%0`. With an argv command pane_pid is the program itself; a one-element
                            command goes through `sh -c`, which exec'd `sleep`, so pane_pid was `sleep`'s pid.
  stderr_missing_pane.txt   `can't find pane: %99`, exit 1, for `send-keys -t %99` and `list-panes -t %99`.
  `load-buffer -` + `paste-buffer -d -r`
                            delivered `a b\nc d` with LF kept and no CR; `send-keys Enter` then added `\r`; the buffer
                            was gone afterwards.
  `select-window -t %1 ; select-pane -t %1`
                            made %1 the active pane.
  a bare `tmux` inside a pane reached that pane's server.

Settled by the live run at 24c6bd1 (reviews/d8-tmux-24c6bd1.log, 42 checks passed, private server, symlinked /bin/cat
stubs named claude and codex):
  stub agents through the process-tree walk
                            discovery found the stub claude typed into a shell (depth 1) and the stub codex as the
                            pane's own process in a second session (depth 0); nvim_get_proc reported "claude" and
                            "codex" for the symlinks. A real AI CLI was not run, so what nvim reads as the name of
                            Claude Code is still not confirmed.
  tools installed as scripts
                            D9: for a process nvim names node, nodejs, bun, python, python3, python3.N or Python, one
                            `ps -ww -o args= -p <pid>` call reads the command line and the script's name is matched
                            (lua/sidekick-ultra/procname.lua). "Python" was seen as nvim's name for /usr/bin/python3 on
                            this Mac, and as the basename of its ps argv0. Unit specs only for the rest: the next live
                            run starts a python and a node script stub and checks discovery, and prints their process
                            names.
  stderr_missing_pane.txt   `tmux exited with 1: can't find pane: %999` for a paste-buffer to a missing pane (24c6bd1, as
                            the probe saw). `send` no longer gets there: see display_pane_gone.txt.
  no server                 `list-panes -a` against a socket path with no server returned an empty list and notified
                            nothing. The log does not record which of the two accepted first stderr lines tmux
                            printed. stderr_no_server.txt (`no server running on ...`, a socket nobody answers) and
                            stderr_no_socket.txt (`error connecting to ... (No such file or directory)`) are both
                            hand-written; the first has not been seen from a real tmux.
  paste buffers             none were left in the server after a send (24c6bd1).
  start                     split-window printed the id and pid; the new pane sat in nvim's window (the then-registry
                            focused it afterwards; `actions` focuses now); the one-element command ran through the shell as a quoted word.

Settled by the live run at 58637a7 (reviews/d8-tmux-58637a7.log, 56 checks passed):
  display_pane_gone.txt     `display-message -p -t %999 '#{pane_in_mode}'` for a pane that does not exist: stdout was
                            empty. Exit 0 is inferred (the backend only reads stdout of a successful call, and the log
                            shows its "tmux pane %999 not found" error, not an exit-code error). Stderr was not
                            recorded, so whether tmux printed anything there is unknown. This differs from
                            `send-keys`, `paste-buffer` and `list-panes -t`, which exit 1 with `can't find pane: %N`.
                            The backend reads empty output from the mode check as "pane not found". Because that
                            check runs before load-buffer, a send to a missing pane never reaches paste-buffer or the
                            delete-buffer cleanup in the live run; the cleanup after a failed paste is covered by the
                            spec only.
  copy mode                 with the pane in copy mode (`copy-mode -t %N`, mode count 1), `send` and `submit` left the
                            mode (count 0) and delivered the text and then the echoed line. `copy-mode -q` was only run
                            on a pane in a mode. How paste-buffer itself behaves in a mode was not observed (the mode
                            is always left first).
  raw paste (-S)            a text holding an ESC byte reached the program as the byte: the pane's tty echoed `^[`, no
                            backslash form appeared, and cat's output had the SGR sequence consumed by the terminal.
                            tmux 3.7 is the floor (README, `lua/sidekick-ultra/backends/init.lua`, health warning).

Settled by the U20 probe (reviews/u20-probe-tmux-linked.log, tmux 3.8, private server, no client):
  list_panes_linked.txt     after `link-window -s a:0 -t b:5`, `list-panes -a` printed the pane `%0` twice, same pid, once
                            per session that links its window (`%0 a`, `%1 b`, `%0 b`). The fixture is hand-written in
                            that shape with the plugin's five fields. `list` keeps the first row of a pane id. Which
                            session tmux lists first for a pane was seen for one link only; `list` does not depend on it;
                            `focus` uses the kept session to decide on `switch-client`, which is still unsettled
                            (see display_session.txt).

Settled by the U24 probes (reviews/a2-probe-tmux-fg.log, reviews/a2-probe2-tmux-title.log, tmux 3.8, private server):
  list_panes*.txt           the fifth field `#{pane_current_command}` is the foreground program: `sleep` while it
                            runs in the foreground, the shell while it is suspended (C-z) or run with `&`. It is the
                            kernel short name (`ucomm`): a node that set `process.title` shows `node`, and `sleep`
                            started through a symlink named `claude` shows `sleep`. `list` keeps a pane only when
                            `ps -o ucomm= -p <matched pid>` equals it. list_panes_foreground.txt is hand-written: two
                            panes at a shell, one at node, one at Claude Code, whose `claude` symlink points to the
                            executable `2.1.322` (ucomm `2.1.322`, plugin name `claude`). The ps answers in the
                            specs are hand-written too; no live run has checked the rule end to end. `send` applies
                            the same equality before it pastes. Probed on macOS only: on Linux tmux may read the
                            name from /proc/<pid>/cmdline while `ucomm` is the kernel `comm`, so the two may differ
                            there (unverified).

Not settled; a live run must still show:
  display_session.txt       `display-message -p -t $TMUX_PANE '#{session_name}'` output, and `switch-client -t %N`
                            from a pane in another session. No client is attached to the private server, so the live
                            run logged UNVERIFIABLE; the probe checked focus only inside one session.
  the working-directory fallback
                            `#{pane_start_path}` when `pane_current_path` is empty: the branch was never taken live.
  a real AI CLI             see the stub row above.
